Streaming Lab

The boat docks at the Coral Garden. How long until the player can move, and what happens to the frames while the rest of the island arrives? Choose how the content is loaded, compressed and split.

Coral Garden, mid-range phone. Goal: the player can move within 2 s of docking, and no frame over 16.67 ms once they can.

Lesson 043: loading and streaming

    Lesson 044 · Challenge: predict first, then tap Set up and check

      What this shows

      Async is about the frames

      LoadSceneAsync doesn't make loading much shorter. It keeps the game drawing while it loads, so a loading screen can move.

      Load what's near first

      Splitting the island into chunks lets the player start after 3 of 12 arrive. The rest streams in a little at a time, under the frame budget.

      Shared things go in one place

      Textures used by every chunk must live in one shared bundle. Otherwise each chunk carries its own copy: on disk, in download size and in memory.

      This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 043's numbers: the island is 270 MB unpacked, of which 18 MB are coral textures used everywhere; flash reads 60 MB/s; LZMA bundles are 2/3 of the unpacked size and unpack at 60 MB/s, LZ4 bundles are 0.8 and unpack at 450 MB/s; creating the objects takes 2.0 s of main thread for all 270 MB; the loading screen draws in 2 ms and gameplay frames take 14.5 ms. A real loader overlaps reading, unpacking and creating; here they run one after another so the parts are easy to see.
